response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS t, COUNT(*) AS c FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT t, c, CAST(c AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(c) FROM j) AS share FROM j), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.c) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Executions are inner-joined to orders on recordvault = ordersmark; if recordvault were duplicated across orders, executions would be counted once per matching order row (recordvault is presumed unique).
A NULL ordertune forms its own group and is included in the number of groups when computing the overall average share.
If no group has a share strictly above average (all equal), the query returns a row with NULLs.
